title: Automation-Safe Scripts
description: Two rules for a CI-safe script: never wait for input, and be idempotent. This block shows a hang and its fixes.

steps.description: Two rules make a script CI-safe: never wait for input, and be idempotent. Line 3 breaks the first rule.
`read -p` blocks on stdin. In CI there is no one to press a key, so the runner waits and then times out.
The fix is non-interactive: `</dev/null` sends any stray prompt EOF, so the command proceeds or fails instead of blocking.
The `if` block shows the second rule. It creates the KV namespace only when it is absent, so running the script twice reaches the same end state.
